newsitem.title: CHINA: HK stocks end up on property, red chip rebound.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks end up on property, red chip rebound.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks finished sharply higher on Thursday after a rally in the lagging property sector and a rebound in red chip shares allowed prices to shrug off early losses.
The Hang Seng Index ended on a gain of 135.50 points, or 0.92 percent, at 14,839.23 after falling to a low of 14,549.91.
Turnover was HK$14.76 billion compared with HK$16.59 billion on Wednesday.
"Property stocks may well have been overdone on the downside -- they have underperformed for ages," Howard Gorges, vice chairman at South China Holdings, said of the sector's surge.
The Hang Seng properties sub-index jumped 594.94 points, or 2.50 percent, to 24,427.71.
"Actually the property developers are bringing in good profits. They had excellent sales and are likely to continue having good sales," said Gorges.
The red chip China-Affiliated Corporations Index soared 115.11 points, or 3.75 percent, to 3,185.02 after falling 6.86 percent on Wednesday.
"Red chips have found a level where a bit of confidence has returned to the market," said Miles Remington, sales trader at SocGen-Crosby Securities.
The red-chip index is down 11 percent since it hit a high of 3,569.27 on July 3.

Brokers said investors were not particularly concerned about a newspaper report on Thursday saying Chinese securities regulators would block further red chip listings until after China's 15th Communist Party Congress later this year.
"People who have been waiting around with cash for the next red chip will now buy stocks, which could be why the market bounced a bit on the red chip sector," said Remington.
Shares in China Resources rose HK$1.50 to HK$33.10 and China Merchants gained HK$1.45 to HK$20.80.
Shares in Liu Chong Hing Bank surged HK$4.85 to HK$24.30 before trading in the stock was suspended in the afternoon.
Brokers said there was talk that COSCO (Hong Kong) may raise its five percent stake in the company. COSCO (Hong Kong) officials were not immediately avaiable for comment.

In the property sector, Sun Hung Kai Properties surged HK$3.00 to HK$89.75 and Henderson Land gained HK$2.50 to HK$68.00. New World Development rose HK$1.60 to HK$46.30. It announced on Wednesday that it would transfer its service business to a new holding company.
